questions.question: Which sea separates Africa from the Arabian peninsula?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Red Sea.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Red Sea** separates** Africa **from the **Arabian peninsula.**
 
• The Red Sea is a **seawater inlet** of the Indian Ocean, located between** Africa and the Arabian Peninsula.**
 
• It is over **2250 km long **and **355 km wide** at its widest point.
 
• The Red Sea is an important **shipping route**, connecting **Europe and Asia.**
 
• It is also a popular tourist destination, known for its** clear waters and coral reefs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Caspian Sea **is the **world's largest inland body of water**, located between **Europe and Asia.**
 
• It is bordered by five countries: **Russia, Iran, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, and Azerbaijan.**
 
• The **Black Sea** is a sea between **Eastern Europe and Western Asia**, bordered by **Bulgaria, Georgia, Romania, Russia, Turkey, and Ukraine.**
 
• It is connected to the **Mediterranean Sea** through the **Bosporus Strait and the Dardanelles.**
 
• The **White Sea** is a southern inlet of the **Barents Sea**, located on the **northwest coast of Russia. **
 
• It is an important **fishing and shipping area,** as well as a popular tourist destination.

questions.question: Jeev Milkha Singh is associated with which sport?

• **Running, jumping, throwing, and walking** competitions are all included in the sport of athletics.

questions.question: In which country was the first Olympic Games held in the year 1896?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Greece.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** first Olympic Games** were held in **Greece** in the **year 1896.**
 
• The Games were held in** Athens**, the capital city of** Greece.**
 
• The first modern Olympic Games were organized by the** International Olympic Committee (IOC).**
 
• The Games were held to honor the** ancient Olympic Games**, which were held in Olympia, Greece, from the **8th century BC to the 4th century AD.**
 
• The first modern Olympics had** 14 countries** participating in **43 events,** and the **USA won** the most medals (20).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Egypt** has **never** hosted the Olympic Games.

 
 
• However, Egypt has participated in the modern Olympic Games since **1912.**
 
 
 
• **Japan** has hosted the Olympic Games **three times **- in Tokyo in 1964, in Sapporo in 1972, and in Nagano in 1998.
 
 
• Japan was also scheduled to host the 2020 Olympics, but it was** postponed to 2021** due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
 
 
• **Italy** has hosted the Olympic Games **twice **- in Rome in 1960 and in Turin in 2006.
 
 
• Italy has also participated in the modern Olympic Games since **1896. **
 
 
 
• The key phrase** "Olympic Games" r**efers to a **multi-sport event** that takes place every **four years.**
 
• The Games feature athletes from **different countries** competing in various sports.
 
• The ancient Olympic Games were held in** Olympia, Greece**, to honor the **Greek god Zeus.**
 
• The Games were **discontinued in 393 AD,** and the modern Olympics were revived in **1896.**

questions.question: Who chairs the Monetary Policy Committee in India?

options.text: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
Deputy Governor, Reserve Bank of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor, Reserve Bank of India.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) **in India is responsible for fixing the **benchmark interest rate** and maintaining **price stability** in the economy.
 
• The MPC consists of **six members**, out of which three are from the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and** three** are appointed by the government.
 
• The Governor of RBI** chairs **the MPC and has the **deciding vote** in case of a tie.
 
• The other two members from** RBI are the Deputy Governor **and an **Executive Director.**
 
• The** three external members** are appointed by the government on the recommendation of a **search-cum-selection committee.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comptroller and Auditor General of India** is responsible for **auditing** the accounts of the government and ensuring **transparency and accountability** in financial transactions.
 
• One of the members from RBI on the MPC is the **Deputy Governor.** However, the Deputy Governor is** not** the chairperson of the MPC.
 
• The **Finance Minister** is responsible for presenting the **annual budget and formulating economic policies **in consultation with the RBI.

questions.question: Jyotiba Phule founded which of the following organizations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satyashodhak Samaj.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jyotiba Phule** founded the **Satyashodhak Samaj organization.**
 
• Satyashodhak Samaj was founded in **1873 **with the aim to **uplift the lower castes **and **women** in society.
 
• The organization also worked towards eradicating social evils like **caste system, untouchability, and child marriage.**
 
• Jyotiba Phule was also a **social reformer** and played a significant role in the** education of women and Dalits **in Maharashtra.
 
• **Arya Samaj, Satnami Samaj, and Brahmo Samaj** were also social reform movements founded in India, but they were not founded by Jyotiba Phule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arya Samaj **was founded by **Swami Dayanand Saraswati** in **1875 **and worked towards the revival of **Vedic culture and education.**
 
• **Satnami Samaj** was founded in **1657 **by **Guru Ghasidas** and aimed to **uplift the lower castes** in society.
 
• **Brahmo Samaj** was founded by** Raja Ram Mohan Roy** in **1828 **and worked towards the** reform of Hindu society **and the promotion of **monotheistic beliefs.**

questions.question: The term "Vetti" in Chola empire is related to ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**forced labour.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **"Vetti" in Chola empire** refers to **forced labor,** which was a common practice during that time.
 
• It was a system where people were forced to work for the government or landlords without any** pay or compensation.**
 
• This system was prevalent in various parts of India during the** medieval period** and was used to build** infrastructure, temples, and other public works.**
 
• The practice of Vetti was **abolished** by the British in the **19th century.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part payments **could refer to a system of payment where a part of the payment is made in** cash** and the rest in kind or **services.**

 
 
• This was also prevalent during the **medieval period **in India.
 
 
 
• **Gold coins** were a form of currency used during the **Chola empire **and were minted by the government.
 
• The **army** was an important institution during the Chola empire and played a crucial role in **expanding their territory **and **maintaining law and order.**

questions.question: Cotton was probably grown at Mehrgarh from about ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 7000 years ago.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cotton was probably grown at **Mehrgarh** from about **7000 years ago**, according to **archaeological evidence.**
 
• This indicates that cotton cultivation in **South Asia** has a long history, and it was one of the earliest regions where cotton was grown.
 
• The discovery of cotton cultivation at Mehrgarh also suggests that the** Indus Valley Civilization, **which developed later in the same region, may have inherited this practice from earlier cultures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Cotton is a** soft, fluffy fiber **that grows in a** boll, or protective capsule**, around the seeds of cotton plants.
 
• Mehrgarh is an archaeological site situated in** Balochistan, Pakistan,** and is one of the earliest sites with** evidence of farming and herding **in South Asia.

questions.question: Which among the following are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bryophyte.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bryophyte** are also known as **amphibians** of the **plant kingdom** because they can survive on** both land and water.**
 
• Bryophytes are **non-vascular plants** that lack true roots, stems, and leaves.
 
• They reproduce through **spores **and are found in **damp and shady places.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thallophytes** are a group of plants that include **algae, fungi, and lichens.**

 
 
• They **lack differentiated tissues and organs** and are found in diverse habitats.
 
 
 
• **Angiosperms **are **flowering plants** that have seeds enclosed in a fruit.
 
 
• They are the most diverse and widespread group of plants and include **trees, shrubs, herbs, and grasses.**
 
 
 
• **Gymnosperms **are **non-flowering plants** that have seeds not enclosed in a fruit.
 
 
• They include **conifers, cycads, and ginkgo** trees and are mostly found in cold and dry regions.

questions.question: Which among the following terms means growing of fruits?

• **Pomiculture** refers to the cultivation of** fruit-bearing trees and plants.**

• **Apiculture** is important for **pollination of crops and plants**, in addition to honey production.
 
• **Arboriculture** involves the **care and maintenance of trees **and shrubs in urban, suburban, and rural areas.
 
• **Sericulture** is an important industry in countries like** China, India, and Japan, **where silk production has a long history.

questions.question: Which two head rivers merge to form the river Ganga?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alaknanda and Bhagirathi.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **two head rivers** that merge to form the river **Ganga **are **Alaknanda and Bhagirathi.**
 
• Alaknanda originates from the** glacier of Satopanth** and Bhagirathi originates from the **glacier of Gangotri.**
 
• The confluence of these two rivers is at **Devprayag in Uttarakhand.**
 
• From Devprayag, the river is known as the Ganga and it flows through several states of India before meeting the** Bay of Bengal **in the** east. **
 
• The river Ganga is considered **sacred by Hindus** and is worshipped as a **goddess.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Alaknanda and Mandakini are **two separate rivers** that flow through Uttarakhand and merge with each other at **Rudraprayag** to form the river Ganga.
 
• Mandakini and Dhauliganga are also** two separate rivers **that merge with Alaknanda at **Rudraprayag **to form the river Ganga.
 
• Bhagirathi and Mandakini are again two separate rivers, but Mandakini **does not **merge with Bhagirathi to form the Ganga.
 
• Instead, Mandakini merges with Alaknanda at **Rudraprayag.**

questions.question: The Lok Sabha (House of the People) was duly constituted for the first time on __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**17 April 1952.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Lok Sabha** is the** lower house **of the Indian Parliament and represents the **people of India.**
 
• The first Lok Sabha was constituted on** April 17, 1952**, after the first general elections held in **1951-52.**
 
• The **Constituent Assembly of India** had adopted the Constitution on** November 26, 1949,** and it came into effect on **January 26, 1950, **marking the beginning of a new era in Indian history.
 
• However, the first general elections were held in **1951-52**, and it took some time to set up the Lok Sabha and other institutions of democracy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1951-1952 **represents the year when the **first general elections** were held.
 
• **Sukumar Sen** was chosen to serve as the** first Chief Election Commissioner** in **March 1950.**
 
• The **Representation of the People Act**, which outlined the procedures for elections to the Houses of Parliament and the Houses of Legislature in each state, was passed by the Indian Parliament a month later.
 
• It was carried out in accordance with the **Indian Constitution's rules,** which were adopted on November 26, 1949.
 
• **1950** represents the year when the **Constitution** came into effect.
 
• The Indian Constitution is the** country's highest law.**
 
• Based on the proposal put forth by** M.N. Roy,** the document establishes the framework that defines the **fundamental political code, structure, procedures, powers, and duties** of governmental institutions as well as the **fundamental rights, guiding principles, and obligations of citizens. **

questions.question: Which article of the Indian constitution provides freedom to manage its own affairs in matters of religion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 26.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 26** of the Indian constitution provides** freedom to manage its own affairs **in matters of **religion.**
 
• This means that every religious denomination or any section thereof has the right to** establish and maintain institutions** for **religious and charitable purposes, **manage its own affairs in matters of religion, and own and acquire **movable and immovable property.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 21** of the Indian constitution guarantees the **protection of life and personal liberty. **
 
• **Article 15** prohibits discrimination on the grounds of **religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.** 
 
• **Article 37** is a provision contained in this Part shall not be enforceable by any court, but the principles therein laid down are nevertheless fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.

questions.question: What is the atomic number of Nitrogen in the science periodic table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **atomic number **of an element is the **number of protons** present in the** nucleus** of an **atom **of that element.
 
• Nitrogen has** 7 protons** in its** nucleus,** hence its **atomic number is 7.**
 
• The atomic number is a **unique identifier **for each element and is used to** arrange elements** in the periodic table.
 
• The symbol for Nitrogen in the periodic table is **'N'** and it belongs to **group 15 and period 2**. 
 
• Nitrogen is a **non-metallic element **and is found in the atmosphere as a** diatomic gas (N2).**
 
• Nitrogen is an essential component of **amino acids, proteins, and nucleic acids** and is also used in the production of **fertilizers, explosives, and other chemical compounds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **11** is the atomic number of **Sodium (Na)** which belongs to **group 1 and period 3 **in the periodic table.
 
• **18** is the atomic number of **Argon (Ar) **which belongs to **group 18 and period 3 **in the periodic table.
 
• **21 **is the atomic** number of Scandium (Sc), **which belongs to **group 3 and period 4 in the periodic table.**

questions.question: Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam is associated with which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam** is associated with the** Kuchipudi dance** form.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Bharatanatyam **is a classical dance form from **Tamil Nadu,** known for its expressive gestures and rhythmic footwork.

questions.question: If Birth rate of a country is more than death rate then the population will ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**increase.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• If the** birth rate** of a country is** more **than the **death rate**, then the population will** increase** as more people are being born than dying.
 
• This is known as** population growth** and can have both **positive and negative** effects on a country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• If the population **grows too quickly**, it can put a **strain **on **resources **such as food, water, and housing. 
 
• However, if the population growth is **managed properly**, it can lead to **economic growth and development.**
 
• The population will** not remain constant** if the birth rate is** higher** than the death rate.
